options: стул
стула
стуле
стулом
cases.translation: Yasha carefully puts the tray down on a chair.
cases.explain: «На» with a verb of placing (ставит) shows motion onto a surface, so it takes the accusative; стул is inanimate, so the accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: На ___ октябрь, а солнечно и тихо, как летом.
options: двор
двора
дворе
двором
cases.translation: It is October outside, yet it is sunny and still, like summer.
cases.explain: The fixed phrase «на дворе» (outside, out of doors) describes location, not motion, so «на» takes the prepositional.

options: Харьков
Харькова
Харькове
Харьковом
cases.translation: And I have to get to Kharkov.
cases.explain: «В» meaning motion towards a destination takes the accusative; Харьков is inanimate, so its accusative equals the nominative.

options: карман
кармана
кармане
карманом
cases.translation: Here it is, right here in my pocket.
cases.explain: «В» showing where something is located (no motion) takes the prepositional.

options: десятина
десятины
десятин
десятинам
cases.translation: In the spring I sowed a thousand desyatinas of poppies.
cases.explain: After the quantity word «тысяча» the counted noun stands in the genitive plural.

options: Париж
Парижа
Париже
Парижем
cases.translation: Send me a letter from Paris.
cases.explain: The preposition «из» (out of, from) always governs the genitive.

cases.sentence: Я к Рагулиным поспею сегодня, не опоздать бы только к ___.
options: поезд
поезда
поезду
поездом
cases.translation: I will get to the Ragulins today, if only I am not late for the train.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, in time for) governs the dative.

options: жизнь
жизни
жизнью
жизней
cases.translation: A new life is beginning, mama!
cases.explain: «Жизнь» is the subject of the verb начинается, and subjects stand in the nominative.

options: селедка
селедки
селедке
селедкой
cases.translation: Who is it that smells of herring?
cases.explain: The impersonal verb «пахнет» names the smell in the instrumental: пахнет селедкой.

options: заботы
забот
заботам
заботами
cases.translation: I am leaving with two worries.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» in the sense of accompaniment takes the instrumental, and the noun agrees with «двумя».

reading.ru: Простой народ прощаться пришел.
reading.question: Who has come to the house at the start of the act, according to Yasha?
options: The common folk, to say goodbye
The buyers of the estate
A group of musicians
The doctors sent for Firs
reading.correct: The common folk, to say goodbye
reading.explain: Yasha announces that the peasants have come to take their leave, adding that they are kind but understand little.

reading.ru: Ты отдала им свой кошелек, Люба.
reading.question: Why does Gaev reproach Lyubov Andreevna?
options: Because she gave the peasants her purse
Because she refused to speak to them
Because she cried in front of them
Because she promised them work
reading.correct: Because she gave the peasants her purse
reading.explain: Gaev says twice that it cannot be done; Lyubov answers only that she could not help herself.

reading.ru: Из города не догадался привезть, а на станции нашел только одну бутылку.
reading.question: Where did Lopakhin get the champagne he offers?
options: He found one bottle at the station
He brought a case from town
Pishchik gave it to him
It was left in the house cellar
reading.correct: He found one bottle at the station
reading.explain: He explains he forgot to bring any from town and picked up a single bottle at the railway station.

reading.ru: Это шампанское не настоящее, могу вас уверить.
reading.question: What does Yasha say about the champagne after drinking it?
options: That it is not the real thing
That it is the best he has tasted
That it is too warm to drink
That it came from Paris
reading.correct: That it is not the real thing
reading.explain: Yasha drinks it and assures the others that the champagne is fake.

reading.ru: Не топили сегодня, все равно уезжаем.
reading.question: Why is the house so cold?
options: The stoves were not lit because everyone is leaving
The windows have all been taken out
A hard frost has set in early
The firewood was sold with the estate
reading.correct: The stoves were not lit because everyone is leaving
reading.explain: Yasha explains there was no heating that day since they are departing anyway.

reading.ru: Господа, имейте в виду, до поезда осталось всего сорок шесть минут!
reading.question: How much time is left before the train when Lopakhin checks his watch?
options: Forty-six minutes
Twenty minutes
Six minutes
An hour and a half
reading.correct: Forty-six minutes
reading.explain: Lopakhin announces forty-six minutes to the train, which means leaving for the station in twenty.

reading.ru: Черт его знает, где мои калоши.
reading.question: What is Trofimov searching for as they prepare to leave?
options: His galoshes
His travelling money
His books
His overcoat
reading.correct: His galoshes
reading.explain: Trofimov hunts for his galoshes throughout the act; Varya finally points them out beside the suitcase.

reading.ru: В Харькове проживу всю зиму.
reading.question: Where does Lopakhin plan to spend the winter?
options: In Kharkov
In Moscow
In Paris
On the estate
reading.correct: In Kharkov
reading.explain: Lopakhin says he is going to Kharkov on the same train and will live there all winter.

reading.ru: Отвыкни от этой привычки — размахивать.
reading.question: What parting advice does Trofimov give Lopakhin?
options: To break the habit of waving his arms about
To stop lending money to friends
To finish his education
To keep the cherry orchard standing
reading.correct: To break the habit of waving his arms about
reading.explain: Trofimov tells him not to wave his arms, and extends the image to his plans for building summer cottages.

reading.ru: Я за перевод получил.
reading.question: How does Trofimov say he got the money in his pocket?
options: He was paid for a translation
He borrowed it from Pishchik
His father sent it
He won it at cards
reading.correct: He was paid for a translation
reading.explain: When Lopakhin insists he has nothing, Trofimov replies that he was paid for a translation.

reading.ru: Дай мне хоть двести тысяч, не возьму.
reading.question: How does Trofimov respond to Lopakhin's offer of money?
options: He refuses, saying he would not take even two hundred thousand
He takes it and promises to repay it
He asks for a smaller sum instead
He tells Lopakhin to give it to Varya
reading.correct: He refuses, saying he would not take even two hundred thousand
reading.explain: Trofimov calls himself a free man over whom money has no power at all.

reading.ru: Я весной посеял маку тысячу десятин, и теперь заработал сорок тысяч чистого.
reading.question: How did Lopakhin make forty thousand that year?
options: By sowing a thousand desyatinas of poppies
By selling the cherry orchard timber
By leasing land to some Englishmen
By taking a post at the bank
reading.correct: By sowing a thousand desyatinas of poppies
reading.explain: He describes the poppies in bloom as a fine sight and says the crop cleared him forty thousand.

reading.ru: Мама вас просит: пока она не уехала, чтоб не рубили сада.
reading.question: What does Anya ask on her mother's behalf?
options: That the orchard not be cut down until her mother has left
That the train be held for a few minutes
That Firs be taken to the hospital at once
That Lopakhin postpone the sale
reading.correct: That the orchard not be cut down until her mother has left
reading.explain: Anya passes on Lyubov Andreevna's request, and Trofimov and Lopakhin hurry out to stop the axes.

reading.ru: Долголетний Фирс, по моему окончательному мнению, в починку не годится, ему надо к праотцам.
reading.question: What is Epikhodov's opinion of Firs?
options: That he is beyond repair and ready to join his forefathers
That he should be given a pension
That he is only pretending to be ill
That he should travel to Paris with the family
reading.correct: That he is beyond repair and ready to join his forefathers
reading.explain: Epikhodov delivers this as his final opinion and adds that he can only envy the old man.

reading.ru: Скажите, мать его пришла, хочет проститься с ним.
reading.question: What message does Varya send to Yasha?
options: That his mother has come to say goodbye to him
That his luggage is still unpacked
That Lyubov Andreevna is calling for him
That the horses are ready
reading.correct: That his mother has come to say goodbye to him
reading.explain: Yasha only waves the news away, saying such people wear out his patience.

reading.ru: Через шесть дней я опять в Париже.
reading.question: What does Yasha tell Dunyasha about his plans?
options: That he will be back in Paris in six days
That he will stay in town for the winter
That he will write to her every week
That he is going to work for Lopakhin
reading.correct: That he will be back in Paris in six days
reading.explain: He says they will board the express train tomorrow and be gone, and that Russia is not for him.

reading.ru: Приехали ко мне англичане и нашли в земле какую-то белую глину…
reading.question: Where did Pishchik suddenly get money to repay his debts?
options: Englishmen found white clay on his land
He sold his horses at the fair
His daughter Dashenka married well
He won a lawsuit in town
reading.correct: Englishmen found white clay on his land
reading.explain: Pishchik arrives out of breath and hands over four hundred roubles each to Lopakhin and Lyubov Andreevna.

reading.ru: Сдал им участок с глиной на двадцать четыре года…
reading.question: For how long did Pishchik lease the clay plot to the Englishmen?
options: Twenty-four years
Twelve years
Forty years
Four years
reading.correct: Twenty-four years
reading.explain: He answers Lopakhin's question and then rushes off to pay his other creditors.

reading.ru: Вторая моя печаль — Варя.
reading.question: What are the two worries Lyubov Andreevna says she is leaving with?
options: The sick Firs and Varya's future
Money and the journey to Paris
Gaev's new job and Anya's exams
The orchard and the family debts
reading.correct: The sick Firs and Varya's future
reading.explain: She names the ailing Firs first, then Varya, who is pale and thin and cries without work to do.

reading.ru: Покончим сразу — и баста, а без вас я, чувствую, не сделаю предложения.
reading.question: What does Lopakhin say about proposing to Varya?
options: That he feels he cannot do it without Lyubov Andreevna's help
That he has already proposed and been refused
That he intends to wait until spring
That he does not want to marry at all
reading.correct: That he feels he cannot do it without Lyubov Andreevna's help
reading.explain: He agrees to settle the matter at once, but says he will not make the offer unless she is there.

reading.ru: Договорилась к ним смотреть за хозяйством… в экономки, что ли.
reading.question: What position has Varya arranged for herself?
options: Looking after the household for the Ragulins, as a sort of housekeeper
A place as a governess in town
Work in the bank alongside Gaev
A post on Lopakhin's new building sites
reading.correct: Looking after the household for the Ragulins, as a sort of housekeeper
reading.explain: She tells Lopakhin she is going to the Ragulins, about seventy versts away at Yashnevo.

reading.ru: В прошлом году об эту пору уже снег шел, если припомните, а теперь тихо, солнечно.
reading.question: What does Lopakhin talk about during the scene alone with Varya?
options: The weather, comparing this autumn with last year's
His feelings for her
The price he paid for the estate
His plans for the summer cottages
reading.correct: The weather, comparing this autumn with last year's
reading.explain: Instead of proposing he speaks about snow, sunshine and three degrees of frost, and Varya answers that their thermometer is broken.

reading.ru: Варя, сидя на полу, положив голову на узел с платьем, тихо рыдает.
reading.question: What does Varya do the moment Lopakhin is called away and hurries out?
options: She sits on the floor and sobs quietly into a bundle of clothes
She runs after him into the yard
She begins packing the last of the luggage
She goes to fetch her mother
reading.correct: She sits on the floor and sobs quietly into a bundle of clothes
reading.explain: A voice calls Lopakhin from the yard, he leaves at once, and Varya breaks down alone.

reading.ru: Про меня забыли…
reading.question: What does Firs realise when he finds the door locked?
options: That they have gone and forgotten about him
That the hospital cart is waiting outside
That the house has already been sold
That Varya has hidden the keys
reading.correct: That they have gone and forgotten about him
reading.explain: He tries the handle, finds it locked, and sits down on the sofa saying it does not matter.

reading.ru: Жизнь-то прошла, словно и не жил…
reading.question: What does Firs say about his life as he lies down?
options: That it has gone by as though he had never lived at all
That it has been long and happy
That he wishes he had gone to Paris
That he expects the family to come back
reading.correct: That it has gone by as though he had never lived at all
reading.explain: He mutters that his strength is gone, nothing is left, and calls himself a good-for-nothing.

reading.ru: Слышится отдаленный звук, точно с неба, звук лопнувшей струны, печальный.
reading.question: What is heard at the very end of the act?
options: A distant sound like a snapped string, and an axe on wood in the orchard
The whistle of the departing train
Singing from the road outside
The peasants returning to the house
reading.correct: A distant sound like a snapped string, and an axe on wood in the orchard
reading.explain: After Firs falls still, the sound of the breaking string is followed by silence and the axe far off in the orchard.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells where Lopakhin got the champagne he is offering?
sentences: Пожалуйте, покорнейше прошу!
По стаканчику на прощанье.
Из города не догадался привезть, а на станции нашел только одну бутылку.
Пожалуйте!
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence explains that he failed to bring any from town and found a single bottle at the station.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how long Lopakhin intends to stay in Kharkov?
sentences: А мне в Харьков надо.
Поеду с вами в одном поезде.
В Харькове проживу всю зиму.
Я все болтался с вами, замучился без дела.
Не могу без работы, не знаю, что вот делать с руками; болтаются как-то странно, точно чужие.
highlight.explain: The third sentence states that he will live in Kharkov for the whole winter.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells Dunyasha when Yasha expects to be in Paris again?
sentences: Через шесть дней я опять в Париже.
Завтра сядем в курьерский поезд и закатим, только нас и видели.
Даже как-то не верится.
Здесь не по мне, не могу жить… ничего не поделаешь.
Насмотрелся на невежество — будет с меня.
highlight.explain: The opening sentence gives the six days after which he will be back in Paris.

highlight.question: Which sentence predicts what will happen to the house itself?
sentences: Минут через десять давайте уже в экипажи садиться…
Прощай, милый дом, старый дедушка.
Пройдет зима, настанет весна, а там тебя уже не будет, тебя сломают.
Сколько видели эти стены!
Сокровище мое, ты сияешь, твои глазки играют, как два алмаза.
Ты довольна?
highlight.explain: Lyubov Andreevna foretells that after the winter and spring the house will be pulled down.

highlight.question: Which sentence explains where Pishchik's unexpected money came from?
sentences: Событие необычайнейшее.
Приехали ко мне англичане и нашли в земле какую-то белую глину…
Остальные потом.
Сейчас один молодой человек рассказывал в вагоне, будто какой-то… великий философ советует прыгать с крыш…
Вы подумайте!
highlight.explain: The second sentence reports the Englishmen who came and found white clay on his land.

highlight.question: Which sentence states the condition Lopakhin puts on making his proposal to Varya?
sentences: Я сам тоже не понимаю, признаться.
Как-то странно все…
Если есть еще время, то я хоть сейчас готов…
Покончим сразу — и баста, а без вас я, чувствую, не сделаю предложения.
highlight.explain: The last sentence says he will not make the offer unless Lyubov Andreevna is present.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the sound that breaks the silence after the carriages drive away?
sentences: Сцена пуста.
Слышно, как на ключ запирают все двери, как потом отъезжают экипажи.
Становится тихо.
Среди тишины раздается глухой стук топора по дереву, звучащий одиноко и грустно.
highlight.explain: The final sentence names the dull, lonely knock of the axe on wood heard in the stillness.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Firs worrying about Gaev instead of about himself?
sentences: Заперто.
Уехали…
Про меня забыли…
А Леонид Андреич, небось, шубы не надел, в пальто поехал…
Жизнь-то прошла, словно и не жил…
Эх ты… недотепа!..
highlight.explain: Locked in and forgotten, Firs still frets that Gaev has travelled in a coat instead of his fur.
